## Community Coordinated Modeling Center Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information ( CCMC DONKI )
## Message Type: Space Weather Notification - Radiation Belt Enhancement
##
## Message Issue Date: 2026-10-16T13:43:00Z
## Message ID: 20261016-AL-002
##
## Disclaimer: NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center is the United States Government official source for space weather forecasts. This "Experimental Research Information" consists of preliminary NASA research products and should be interpreted and used accordingly.


## Summary:

Significantly elevated energetic electron fluxes in the Earth's outer radiation belt. GOES "greater than 2.0 MeV" integral electron flux is above 1000 pfu starting at 2026-10-16T13:20Z. 

The elevated energetic electron flux levels are caused by the arrival of the coronal hole high speed stream starting on 2026-10-10, reaching maximum sustained speeds of approximately 850 km/s. The solar wind speed observed at L1 is currently around 445 km/s. The elevated energetic electron flux levels may also be associated with the combined arrival of CME with ID 2026-10-08T16:24:00-CME-001 and CME with ID 2026-10-08T16:53:00-CME-001. These CMEs and the coronal hole high speed stream were detected at L1 by SOLAR-1 at 2026-10-10T14:33Z (see notification 20261010-AL-001). The energetic electron flux levels may have been further enhanced by the arrival of CME with ID 2026-10-10T16:15:00-CME-001 detected at L1 by SOLAR-1 at 2026-10-13T00:21Z (see notification 20261013-AL-001).

NASA spacecraft at GEO, MEO and other orbits passing through or in the vicinity of the Earth's outer radiation belt can be impacted.

Activity ID: 2026-10-16T13:20:00-RBE-001. 

## Notes: 
The coronal hole high speed stream starting on 2026-10-10, the CME with ID 2026-10-08T16:24:00-CME-001, as well as the CME with ID 2026-10-08T16:53:00-CME-001 are associated with the geomagnetic storm with ID 2026-10-10T15:00:00-GST-001 (see notifications 20261010-AL-006 and 20261010-AL-007) and modeled magnetopause crossing with ID 2026-10-10T15:33:00-MPC-001 (see notification 20261010-AL-005).

## Community Coordinated Modeling Center Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information ( CCMC DONKI )
## Message Type: Space Weather Notification - CME (BepiColombo, Parker Solar Probe, OSIRIS-APEX)
##
## Message Issue Date: 2026-10-17T13:12:17Z
## Message ID: 20261017-AL-001
##
## Disclaimer: NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center is the United States Government official source for space weather forecasts. This "Experimental Research Information" consists of preliminary NASA research products and should be interpreted and used accordingly.


## Summary:

O-type CME detected by STEREO A / GOES / SOHO. 

Start time of the event: 2026-10-17T02:48Z.

Estimated speed: ~1048 km/s.

Estimated opening half-angle: 38 deg.

Direction (lon./lat.): -99/-4 in Heliocentric Earth Equatorial coordinates.

Activity ID: 2026-10-17T02:48:00-CME-001

Based on preliminary analysis by the Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office and heliospheric modeling carried out at NASA Community Coordinated Modeling Center, it is estimated that the CME may impact BepiColombo, Parker Solar Probe, and OSIRIS-APEX (glancing blow).  The leading edge of the CME will reach BepiColombo at 2026-10-17T21:43Z and Parker Solar Probe at 2026-10-18T16:32Z (plus minus 7 hours). The flank of the CME may reach OSIRIS-APEX at 2026-10-20T04:00Z (plus minus 7 hours).

## Notes: 


SCORE CME typification system:
S-type: CMEs with speeds less than 500 km/s
C-type: Common 500-999 km/s
O-type: Occasional 1000-1999 km/s
R-type: Rare 2000-2999 km/s
ER-type: Extremely Rare >3000 km/s
